items.title: Karolina Strassmayer interviewed by Monk Rowe, May 25, 2023
items.q: Yesterday I did an interview with Roscoe Mitchell.

ctx.x: years as I’ve grown as a human being I have discovered that giving with music is a great privilege. It is an experience that we can give people and what I give is actually this — what moves me, my idea of beauty, but also when I’m on stage I’m somebody who is present. I’m present for the music and for the people in that moment. And that’s really at the center. It doesn’t matter the notes, the style or this or that. It is am I here? Am I really here? Am I really present for this? And that is a gift and it’s a gift…

Let’s talk about that out a bit. Yesterday I did an interview with Roscoe Mitchell. And I didn’t even — it wasn’t a question but I said something about free jazz. And he was adamant there’s no such thing as free jazz. And I think the reason, well he said it, he says considering how hard I work at this music there’s no such thing as free jazz — and he was almost angry about it. For you, what does free actually mean?

Wow. That is a very deep question. Wow. I’m not sure how to answer that. That is such a wide question. Because if I say okay free means we’re not playing a tune or we’re not playing over a structure, but that’s actually not true either because while I’m playing free music in my head I create a structure and I create something. I create, it’s just a spontaneous structure that I play off of. I can’t answer it, I wish I could. How did he answer it?
